principles: Make the M8 requires3x2 predicate mechanically true only from structured facts, not prose or changed-file names.
Preserve the non-Authority boundary: local host verdicts and local policy facts never set production completion fields.
Prefer a narrow additive policy branch over rewriting existing review escalation or review assurance floor behavior.
Keep diagnostics readable so operators can tell threshold-triggered, explicit-policy, full-3x2, and degraded-single-host states apart.
drivers: Two high gap_analyze entries must disappear for explicitlyConfiguredHighRiskPolicyRequires3x2.
DONE already consumes review_escalation_status and review_assurance_floor; new facts must be gate-visible and contract-protected.
Existing dirty main work from other stories must not be mixed into this story worktree.

options.name: A: Add explicit policy fact support to review escalation and bind it in process-fact coverage
pros: Keeps changed-file/prose classification diagnostic-only unless a structured policy fact exists.
Can be protected with smoke and process-fact contract assertions.
cons: Requires touching command schema, handler, evaluator, process event type, and verification contract.
More surface area than a comment-only traceability fix.

options.name: B: Only add @task metadata mentioning explicitlyConfiguredHighRiskPolicyRequires3x2
pros: Smallest diff and would likely silence gap_analyze.
cons: Would overstate implementation because review_escalation_status still lacks an explicit policy branch.
Does not strengthen future behavior or diagnostics.

options.name: C: Rewrite the roadmap wording to remove the explicit policy predicate
pros: Would align docs with current first-round-threshold-only review escalation.
cons: Does not satisfy the user request to handle the high gaps as implementation coverage.

chosen: A: Add explicit policy fact support to review escalation and bind it in process-fact coverage
rationale: Option A is the only path that resolves the scanner-visible high gaps while also making the M8 predicate real runtime behavior rather than annotation-only coverage.

preMortem.scenario: Changed-file classification accidentally sets explicit high-risk policy 3x2
preMortem.trigger: Implementation reuses high-risk path/touchpoint checks as the explicit policy branch.
preMortem.consequence: Ordinary process-file edits could silently require 3x2 without a configured policy fact, violating the roadmap.
preMortem.mitigation: Only consume an explicit process event/command with policyVersion, storyId, sourcePolicyRef, rolloutStage, risk class or milestone, issuer, timestamp, and current material binding.

preMortem.scenario: Local policy fact is mistaken for Authority completion
preMortem.trigger: Status output or report fields blur local review evidence with production receipt evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Users may believe production Authority Server completion was verified when it was not.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, and productionDone hard false in reports and command output; add contract assertions for those tokens.

preMortem.scenario: Gap disappears but contract can regress later
preMortem.trigger: Only a smoke test covers the exact predicate token, and process-fact registry omits it.
preMortem.consequence: Future edits remove the predicate binding while gap_analyze still misses it.
preMortem.mitigation: Update process-fact-levels/registry rationale and verify-process-fact-contract.mjs to assert the explicit predicate token and consumer gate.

preMortem.scenario: Story merge conflicts with parallel B-5a9a process-fact edits
preMortem.trigger: Both stories edit process-fact registries in nearby lines.
preMortem.consequence: DONE merge may require manual conflict resolution and careful post-merge validation.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep B-963c changes narrow and re-run build, contract, gap_analyze, and convergence_check after merge if conflicts occur.
